question.text:
Consider the given plot of enthalpy of the following reaction between A and B.
A+B→C+D. Identify the incorrect statement.

options.text: Formation of <math><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math> and <math><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></math> from <math><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math> has highest enthalpy of activation.
<math><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math> is the thermodynamically stable product.

Activation enthalpy to form <math><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math> is <math><mn>5</mn><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">k</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">J</mi><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">o</mi><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">l</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> less than that to form <math><mi mathvariant="normal">D</mi><mo>.</mo></math>

solution.text:
A+B→C+D

Activation enthalpy for C=20-0=20 kJ/mol
Activation enthalpy for D=15-5=10 kJ/mol
